newsitem.title: USA: Letter claims responsibility for two Atlanta bombings.
newsitem.headline: Letter claims responsibility for two Atlanta bombings.

text.p: An anonymous letter purported to be from a militant Christian group called the Army of God claimed responsibility on Monday for the recent bombings of an abortion clinic and a gay and lesbian nightclub in Atlanta.

The FBI could not say immediately whether the letter, posted to an international news agency within hours of last Friday night's explosion at a lesbian bar, was a genuine claim of responsibility or sent by a crank.

But investigators said they were aware of a shadowy radical group called the Army of God, which had been known to circulate bomb-making manuals as a means of advocating violence against abortion clinics.
The letter purported to contain details about the makeup of bombs used in both attacks and sought to set up a system by which claims of responsibility could be confirmed after future bombings.
The letter also threatened "total war" against the federal government and promised further attacks on homosexuals, their organisations and supporters.
In a reference to abortion, it lashed out at what it called the annual "murder" of 3.5 million children, saying the practice would not be tolerated.
The letter, postmarked Saturday from an Atlanta branch post office, ended with a promise of death to the "new world order".

In the latest bombing, an explosive device packed with nails went off Friday in the rear patio section of the Otherside Lounge in northeast Atlanta shortly before 10 p.m. EST, injuring five people and sending a young woman to the hospital with a nail in her arm.
In mid-January, a bomb described by FBI agents as being of similar makeup shattered the offices of the Atlanta Family Planning Services centre in the suburb of Sandy Springs.
A second explosive device was left in an outside parking lot in both attacks, as if intended for law enforcement officers and rescue workers responding to the initial emergency call.
At least half a dozen people were injured outside the Sandy Springs abortion clinic when the second bomb went off.
Federal officials, who say the bombings and the deadly Centennial Olympic Park bombings bear similarities, have speculated that a serial bomber may be at large in Atlanta.
